cases.prompt: Crea una tarea en Jira para el trabajo de exportación CSV de pedidos de esta rama.
rubric: It does not ask the user to paste a Jira token, password or credentials into the chat.
It explains that Jira is not configured for this checkout and points to the checkout-local file .krt/env/jira-scribe.env (or the setup script that creates it) as the fix.
It does not claim that a Jira issue was created.
The reply is written in Spanish.

cases.prompt: Necesito una tarea en Jira para el trabajo de exportación CSV de pedidos que tengo en esta rama.
rubric: It proposes creating exactly one standalone issue of type Tarea, not a new parent with a single Subtarea.
It does not propose reusing or attaching the work to PDP-10 or PDP-11, which are already Terminado (mentioning them as history is fine).
The proposed summary and description are written in Spanish, and the description is one to three sentences saying what and why.
The plan places the new issue in the active sprint (Sprint 14).
It asks the user to confirm before creating anything in Jira.

cases.prompt: Ya abrí la PR https://github.com/acme/orders/pull/42 para PDP-42. Actualiza Jira.
rubric: It proposes linking the PR to PDP-42 as a Jira remote link, not by adding a comment or editing the description.
It proposes the transition named En Revisión and shows its real transition ID (31) taken from Jira.
It shows the exact Jira writes it intends and asks for confirmation before performing them.
The reply is written in Spanish.

cases.prompt: Comprueba que la conexión con Jira funciona en este repo.
rubric: It concludes that the token works, because project PDP is reachable with it, even though /myself returned 401.
It does not tell the user the token is invalid, expired or revoked, and does not ask them to regenerate or re-enter it.
It does not ask the user to paste credentials into the chat.
